references.text: The pillar of cloud descended and stood at the entrance to the tent whenever Moses went in, and the Lord spoke with Moses.

When the priests came out of the holy place, the cloud filled the house of the Lord, so that the priests could not stand there to perform their service because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord.

The house of the Lord was filled with a cloud when the priests praised the Lord, and the priests could not stand there to perform their service because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.
The priests could not enter the house of the Lord, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord.
Isaiah sees the glory of the Lord filling the temple, and smoke fills the house, as a parallel to the cloud and the glory of the Lord that filled the tabernacle.
The glory of the Lord rose from above the cherubim to the threshold of the house, and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the glory of the Lord.
Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord filling the temple, as a parallel to the glory of the Lord that filled the tabernacle.
The temple was filled with smoke from God's glory and from his power, and no one could enter the temple, as a parallel to Moses being unable to enter the tent sanctuary.
The same divine manifestation that prevented Moses from entering the tent now prevents the priests in their service at the temple.
A parallel account confirming that the cloud and the glory hindered the priests during the dedication of the temple.
Describes the moment when the cloud filled the house, which is the direct reason why the priests could not later perform their service.
